teaser.text: Union Pacific Corporation is a freight railroad: it sells the movement of other companies’ goods across 23 western U.S. states. To understand its business, follow one journey from the cargo it carries to the customer who buys it, then to the costs that determine what Union Pacific keeps.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Union Pacific?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA rises gradually before the merger, then jumps when Norfolk Southern contributes. The base case uses $13,400 million in October 2027, supported by a 4% standalone growth assumption and improved velocity and dwell. It reaches $19,850 million in October 2028 and $21,400 million in October 2029 as Norfolk Southern and synergies are added. The bear case excludes Norfolk Southern until later and falls to $12,350 million in 2028, reflecting the 2023 decline and traffic risk. The bull case reaches $22,800 million by 2029 because pricing, productivity and synergies all exceed the base path. Management’s EPS outlook supports growth, but it is not EBITDA guidance.

dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Union Pacific's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Union Pacific pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends grow modestly in the base case, from $5.72 to $6.05 per share. That follows the latest $1.42 quarterly rate and the stated commitment to annual increases. The bear case declines from $5.68 to $4.80 as financing, integration and weak earnings force cuts. The bull case reaches $6.33 because stronger earnings permit faster increases, though it remains below an immediate full-synergy payout.

blocks.heading: Is Union Pacific's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The pattern matters because dividends and buybacks are not costless proof of success. A dividend sends cash directly to shareholders. A buyback reduces the number of shares, which can increase each remaining share’s claim on future earnings. But if payouts exceed free cash flow, the gap must come from asset sales, cash reserves or borrowing.

That happened especially strongly early in the period. Union Pacific later retained free cash flow in 2023 and 2024, while debt repayments exceeded new borrowing. Even so, net debt ended 2025 above its level at the end of 2021. Union Pacific also paused repurchases for the Norfolk Southern transaction, allowing more internally generated cash to accumulate for the proposed acquisition.

blocks.heading: What could change Union Pacific's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The view would move toward the bear case if regulatory conditions delay closing, integration costs rise or traffic benefits fail to appear during 2027–2029. Fuel costs rising faster than surcharge recovery would also pressure margins.

earnings.title: Union Pacific earnings: date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Union Pacific reports on October 22, 2026; guidance is high-single-digit reported EPS growth, with traffic and productivity to watch.
earnings.opening: Union Pacific's next results are expected on October 22, 2026. Watch Union Pacific's traffic, revenue excluding fuel recovery and productivity after fuel and wage pressure.
earnings.closing: The full Union Pacific memo also answers questions about Union Pacific's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has Union Pacific guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management now promises faster earnings growth in 2026 while keeping investment high. It raised its full-year outlook to high-single-digit growth in reported earnings per share, or profit attributable to each share. It also reaffirmed high-single- to low-double-digit compound annual growth through 2027. Compound growth means each year builds on the previous year’s larger earnings base.

blocks.heading: Did Union Pacific keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: There is evidence that Vena’s promises have produced operational improvement. Union Pacific reported its best full-year safety performance in 2025, along with records for freight-car velocity and terminal dwell. In the second quarter of 2026, injury and derailment rates improved again, while terminal dwell fell 7% to 19.7 hours. Those results support progress, although they do not prove that the railroad will remain resilient during integration.

blocks.heading: How have Union Pacific's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter showed real improvement, but fuel made the operating trend harder to see. Revenue rose 11.5%, while operating income rose 9.4%. Net income increased 6.2%, and diluted EPS rose 6.7%.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Union Pacific's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next earnings report will test whether the raised outlook is becoming more credible. Union Pacific releases third-quarter results on October 22, 2026. Investors should watch traffic, revenue excluding fuel recovery and productivity after fuel and wage pressure.
